firstImpressions: Before source or diagnostics, the opening circular made two saffron to Fogmouth understandable. It gave a unit quote, age, travel time, downside estimate and buyer warning. One eel to Saint Mire was within reach. The late-appearing tour caught my first attempted tap. I skipped it and completed the trade from the market and map cues.
method: Two fresh direct-file WebKit contexts, 390 × 844 with mobile touch, port 9573. I chose the trades below and inspected the visible market, route, harbor, event and ending screens. Normal opening timing. My temporary helper tapped visible controls and typed quantities. From N3 of run one and N2 of run two it enabled FAST for routine travel. It used the harness public-observation route policy for intervening nights, bought at most its first suggested line, sold profitable cargo and handled routine events. It did not use finance or dock work. These intervening decisions are scripted coverage. No run-state fixtures in either phone voyage. Diagnostics and fixtures were separate, after first impressions. All evidence was generated in this review.
decisions: Buy two saffron at 859 and keep 782. One eel at 2,073 toward Saint Mire offered +52% but left only 427. Fogmouth was one night, risk 4/5, with a fresh 1,377 sighting.
Fogmouth had a buyer at 1,837. Sold both for 3,674, gross gain 1,956.
After selling, buy one eel at 2,610 for Saint Mire on a one-night-old +21% sighting. Keeping cash and heading back toward the lender would protect the opening profit.
Arrived N3 at 2,866. The 256 quote gain was smaller than the cutter bribe of 853.

Liquidate one chip at 3,942 against 3,144 cost. Repay 4,000 of overdue debt and send eight rain at 153 toward Saint Mire. Eleven rain fit the circular's plan, but would leave only 353 after repayment. Eight left 812.
Rain arrived at 176 against the remembered 210. Sold eight for 1,408. Debt grew from 6,747 to 7,422.
Switch from eight rain to four saffron at 491 for Lanternquay, seen at 933 one night ago. Holding rain for the N13–16 Saint Mire fleet call would avoid a loaded voyage but cost another night.
The cutter took two saffron. A leak took another. Lanternquay had no buyer for the survivor. The next collector took the remaining cargo and cash against debt.
After spending N22 dock-working from zero cash, buy six kelp at 44 and keep 86. Two rain at 166 would concentrate the 350 stake and leave just 18. Take kelp to Lanternquay.
Six arrived worth 288 at 48 each, a gain of 24. In the same interval the debt reached 20,656.

With 542, one night left and no chance to reroute a missed sale, split the load between two rain at 152 and five kelp at 37. The circular offered three rain to Lanternquay at a remembered 242. Both goods had recent buyers there.
Both sold on N30. Rain fetched 196 and kelp 52. The mixed basket realized 652 against 489 spent, beating the three-rain alternative's 132 gross gain at those same unit prices. Cash closed at 705.
observations: Trade (92). Six decisions above. N11 the reserve competed directly with interest savings. N29 two dated quotes justified splitting a small purse on the last crossing. The second run's full 30-slot hold at N6 made unloading necessary to buy anything. The main circular suggests just one load, so competing baskets require reading individual rows.

Routes (91). Seven named districts on lit canal links, eight goods, row sparklines, dated sightings and an explicit missing-buyer warning. Fogmouth offered one night at risk 4/5. On the replay, the Exchange offered one night at 2/5 and the lender later offered one night at 1/5. Before wireless, saffron 1,377 became 1,837, the eel's +21% became +10%, rain 210 became 176, and saffron 933 had no buyer. Fleet dates are dependable, the +40% demand modifier does not fix the arrival quote. The illustrative haircut cannot express a zero-sale arrival in its profit number.

Economy (86). First run traded with borrowed funds then repaid late. Replay reduced principal at departure and paid off N7 while retaining a trading stake. Keyboard coverage bought hold, motor and wireless and banked funds. In the matched N11 test, debt repayment dominated passive banking while overdue. I did not compare upgrade-first and debt-first from the same state, or establish their relative return across seeds.

Risk (92). N2 cutter bribe of 853 protected the eel. N12 accepting inspection plus jettison reduced four saffron to one. In replay N6 the same inspection found nothing in an empty hold, saving the offered 1,792 bribe. The gull offered certain cash loss against a 70% chance to save the bag and a hull penalty on failure. Separate fixtures verified both outcomes. N22 dock work after losing the entire stake paid 350, consumed a night and raised debt from 17,071 to 18,778. It restored access to trade but barely affected the prospect of solvency.

Pacing (83). Opening reserves, late-rate principal and final-night liquidation generated different decisions. N14–22 the routine policy repeatedly sailed empty instead of taking the available recovery action. This stretch cannot establish meaningful choices every two nights. Even after returning to trade, a 24 gain on kelp was dwarfed by nearly 1,900 in overnight interest. Settlement clearly reconciled 705 cash minus 36,593 debt to −35,888, Drowned Debtor, exactly 35,888 short of Bilge Rat.

Replay (91). On the second opening the best saffron lead moved to Orchid. I repaid 500 and chose three pearls at 524 for the Exchange, risk 2/5, quote 723. They arrived at 741. By N6 a different fleet window had put 30 rain bought at 125 in a 352 market. I sold all 30 for 10,560, sailed empty to Lanternquay, accepted a free inspection and cleared 7,803 debt on N7. N10 had 4,330 cash, zero debt and two chips worth 12,454. A wireless-first run with money retained for trades is another plausible approach. Intermediate portfolio growth was helper-driven, including the rain purchase.

Onboarding (87). The circular, map's Sail action, and sale sheet completed the opening loop without external explanations. Average cost, fleet demand, quote age and the missing-dealers row explained both the big saffron gain and the later failed sale. The 15% reserve note explained the preset quantity. The tour appeared after the market looked interactive. I did not complete or assess every tour step.

Input (89). Both touch contexts and 1280 × 800 desktop worked. The keyboard-only run settled with zero pointer events and 4,130 navigation Tab presses under the harness strategy. Mouse coverage included trade, selecting a route, a gull choice and settlement. Phone audits of the replay N6 sale sheet, lender route and cutter, plus first-run ending, found zero on-screen targets below 44 px and zero estimated normal-text contrast failures. Selected-map, event and ending screenshots showed amber focus rings. Amounts, signs, text and sparklines supplemented color. Reduced-motion harness checks covered the title. Trade-sheet focus-ring appearance and all motion transitions were not individually verified.

World (86). The crane at Copperhook, Fogmouth seawall, Quill's lender copy and a gull tethered to the captain's wrist make the canals recognizable. A sale showed proceeds and profit, travel gave a named night card, and an empty-hold inspection explicitly reported finding nothing. All three were legible without the log. Repeated trade sheets require reopening each good and choosing its mode. Source defines different buy, sell, voyage and ending cues. The phone audio stand-in counted 570 starts while running, zero suspended. A touch toggled mute on in the replay. Audible mix and ordinary-speed pacing across a full run remain untested.

Reliability (92). Exact frozen file, 258,584 bytes. Source and runtime checks found inline vanilla delivery, guarded storage and zero external requests in instrumented runs. Direct-file phone play finished with no reported errors and the −35,888 ledger entry survived a fresh navigation. The independent offline keyboard run reconciled 72,349 cash + 174,161 vault to 246,510 and persisted. verify.cjs passed corrupt storage and sandboxed allow-scripts boot with same-origin denied. Quantities reconciled in opening and closing trades. Sandbox coverage reached start, not settlement.

matchedCheck.kind: Independent deterministic Chromium finance fixture, with actual mouse services and one simulated advanceDay per branch
matchedCheck.start: Cloned N11 Lanternquay state after chip liquidation, cash 6,036, debt 10,747, bank zero. Both branches allocate 4,000 and advance one identical market night.
matchedCheck.finding: Repayment was 340 ahead after one night with identical cash liquidity. Banking earned 60 while leaving 400 in avoidable interest. This tests a passive allocation, not every possible shortcut.

priorities: Show the next night's interest alongside the dock-work payout and the projected cash left to trade. A broke captain should see both the immediate recovery and the cost in net worth.
Let the route card compare a mixed hold with the suggested single-good load, including the proceeds if one buyer is absent. N29 required assembling that comparison from separate rows.
Show the tour before the opening market accepts taps. Give skipped-tour players the same immediate route from a purchased good to its dated destination quote.
limits: WebKit on Windows emulates touch, not physical iPhone Safari, its software keyboard, safe areas, toolbar or audio hardware. Contrast audit averages gradients. Sound operation and listening quality were assessed separately.

No other panel outputs used. Keyboard seed 31, verify.cjs, event-check.cjs and the matched finance test are supplementary scripted or fixture evidence. The other judges' strategies and results were unknown.

Full denial-of-storage settlement, every market shock, every rank and the design notes were not independently inspected. NOTES.md was outside the allowed source packet. No exhaustive strategy or shortcut search.
